conviction_note: Q3 FY26's blowout ($176.6M gross profit, $2.09 EPS) came from a retail-premium spike that peaked 2026-02-17 at 19.16% on Silver Eagles; inside the April-June quarter now being reported that premium collapsed to 5.3-7.9% and US Mint Silver Eagle bullion units fell to 640,500 from 8,180,000 in Q3 and 2,620,000 in the year-ago quarter, with May 2026 the first zero month in the program's 40-year history - and the DTC segment that carries 67% of gross profit earns premium x ounces, so at the company's own demonstrated operating leverage (H1 FY26: $166.2M gross profit produced just $10.7M net income) Q4 lands near breakeven and the FY27 $4.09 sell-side anchor breaks; sized at -5.0 rather than the -7.0 sum of findings because findings 1-3 are three data families measuring one phenomenon, and held inside the 8.87% indicative implied move because the wholesale trading desk had a violently volatile silver tape ($89.33 to sub-$60) that can print a large offsetting number.

findings.finding: US Mint American Eagle silver bullion sales in Gold.com's fiscal Q4 (Apr/May/Jun 2026) were 380,500 / 0 / 260,000 coins = 640,500, down 76% from the year-ago quarter's 2,620,000 (1,530,000 / 775,000 / 315,000) and down 92% from Q3 FY26's 8,180,000, with May 2026 the first calendar month of zero bullion Silver Eagle sales in the program's 40-year history - and Gold.com is both a Mint Authorized Purchaser and, since consolidating Sunshine Minting on 2026-04-02, the owner of the Mint's primary silver blank supplier.
findings.source_date: 2026 (May-2026 data month; date verified independently - see independence)
findings.why_not_priced: The Mint publishes this monthly in a CSV that no financial aggregator maps onto GOLD, and the sell-side is visibly modelling the gold price instead: a $70 target was reaffirmed on 2026-08-27, five analysts average $65.80 against a $43.66 spot (+42%), and Zacks ran GOLD as Bull of the Day. If this were in the price, the 25-delta skew would not be +0.59 vol points (effectively flat) and open interest would not be 0.29 puts per call - that is call-dominated positioning, the opposite of a market braced for a retail-volume print. The zero month also lands in the same quarter Gold.com bought the blank supplier whose flagship order book it emptied, which is a fact no wire story has connected.
findings.independence: Date and magnitude corroborated from two different sources: coinnews.net puts YTD-through-June 2026 bullion Silver Eagle sales at roughly 8.8 million ounces, which matches the six monthly figures summing to 8,820,500 exactly (https://www.coinnews.net/2026/07/02/silver-eagle-soars-in-return/, URL path /2026/07/), and a second outlet reports the May zero with 2026 in its URL path (https://atlantagoldandcoin.com/us-mint-zero-silver-eagle-sales-may-2026/). The 2025 comparison months come from the US Mint's own tidy CSV (https://www.usmint.gov/content/dam/usmint/data/tidy/bullion-american-eagle-silver.csv).

findings.finding: The retail premium over spot on 1oz American Silver Eagles - which is Gold.com's actual revenue per ounce, not the metal price - peaked at 19.16% on 2026-02-17 inside fiscal Q3, then fell to a 5.30% low on 2026-04-24, 6.69% on 2026-05-25 and a ~7.93% June average across fiscal Q4, and has kept falling in the current quarter: 8.48% average in July 2026 against 6.87% in August 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Gold.com's own Q3 release states Direct-to-Consumer contributed 67% of gross profit, so gross profit is premium x ounces - yet every piece of published coverage keys off the gold price (gold rose ~10% in August) and off the Q3 headline of $10.35bn revenue and $2.09 EPS. A ~19% premium on ~$80 silver is roughly $15/oz of spread; a 6% premium on ~$69 silver is roughly $4/oz. If the market had focused on this, the August reaffirmation of a $70 price target and the FY27 $4.09 EPS anchor would have been cut instead, and the 20-day run-up would not still be +2.27%. The August print at 6.87%, below July's 8.48%, is the part that matters most because it prices the FY27 outlook management gives on tonight's call, not the quarter already ended.
findings.independence: Same publisher as finding 1 but a different dataset (dealer ask prices vs Mint unit sales) - flagging the source-cluster overlap explicitly. Independent directional corroboration of collapsed premiums from a third party: as of 2026-08-26, silver spot $68.57 with 100oz bars and 90% junk silver quoted at -4.8% (below spot) and 1oz coins at ~0.7% over spot on the lowest-premium screen (https://www.kellergoldandsilver.com/post/why-is-the-buyback-price-for-silver-so-much-lower-than-the-spot-price-right-now-2026-guide).

findings.finding: Third-party e-commerce estimates put jmbullion.com revenue at $66.4M in July 2026 and down 24% over the trailing three months versus the preceding three months, while Similarweb's July 2026 data shows the site's global rank deteriorating from 18,648 to 20,259 over three months and traffic down 3% month-on-month.
findings.why_not_priced: JM Bullion is 27% of Q3 gross profit on the company's own disclosure and is not separately tracked by any sell-side model; alternative-data panels on a private-brand website are not in wire copy and not in the single published EPS estimate. If the market were watching DTC order flow rather than the gold price, the 5-day run of -6.8% would not sit against a 20-day run of +2.27% and a call-heavy option book. This is an estimate from a panel, not a company disclosure, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Yes - a different vendor with a different methodology points the same way: Similarweb's jmbullion.com page (https://www.similarweb.com/website/jmbullion.com/, July 2026 data). Both are independent of the US Mint volume series and the dealer premium series in findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: The company's own nine-month numbers imply extreme operating leverage that makes the lone $0.96 Q4 estimate fragile: 9M gross profit $342.8M less Q3's $176.6M leaves $166.2M for H1, and 9M net income $70.2M less Q3's $59.5M leaves just $10.7M - so at an H1-like ~$83M quarterly gross profit the business earns roughly $0.19 a quarter, against a Q4 cost base now carrying Q3's $78M SG&A plus a full quarter of consolidated Sunshine Minting and $19M+ of quarterly interest.
findings.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on a public release rather than a discovery, but with only one published Q4 estimate the arithmetic has visibly not been done: Zacks' 2026-02-11 note carried FY27 EPS of $4.09 (~$1.02 a quarter) and FY26 estimates raised 50% in 60 days, which extrapolates the premium-spike quarter as a run-rate. If the H1-to-Q3 gross profit swing had been recognised as a premium cycle rather than a level, targets 42-60% above spot would not have been reaffirmed on 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-27.
findings.independence: none - this rests on the same Q3 release as the segment mix cited in findings 2 and 3, and should be collapsed into that source cluster rather than counted twice. The FY27 $4.09 anchor it argues against is separately sourced: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/bull-day-goldcom-gold (2026-02-11).

Any preliminary release, guidance pre-announcement, auditor change, delayed-filing notice or material-weakness disclosure between 2026-05-11 and 2026-09-02 - EDGAR shows only Form 4s (Jun 18, Jul 1, Jul 6), a 13D/A (May 7), a 13G (Aug 14) and the May shelf registrations

baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline's positioning rather than agreeing with it: the 25-delta skew is only +0.59 vol points, put/call open interest is 0.29 (call-dominated), the 20-day run-up is still positive and both prints in the reaction history went up - so the option market and the sell-side are leaning the opposite way to a retail premium-and-volume collapse that is measurable in Mint data and dealer prices and is still worsening in August.
